κατατετέλεκεν ὁ Ἰσραὴλ προφητῶν ἁγίων δίχα.
Γεγόνασι μὲν γὰρ αἰχμάλωτοι κατὰ καιροὺς, καὶ εἰς τὴν Περσῶν καὶ Μήδων
ἀπῴχοντο χώραν γυ- ναιξὶν ὁμοῦ καὶ φιλτάτοις. Πλὴν οὐ δίχα προφητῶν ἁγίων
κατέβησαν εἰς Αἴγυπτον, ᾑρηκότων κατὰ και- ροὺς τὴν διαβόητον Ἱερουσαλὴμ τῶν
Βαβυλωνίων, ἀλλὰ συνῆν αὐτοῖς ὁ προφήτης Ἱερεμίας, τοῖς ἄνω- θεν καὶ παρὰ
Θεοῦ διακονούμενος λόγοις. Ἐπειδὴ δὲ πεπαρῳνήκασιν εἰς Χριστὸν, ἔρημοι
φραγμοῦ διατε- τελέκασι, καὶ πᾶσα αὐτῶν ἀσφάλεια πέπτωκεν. Τοῦτο γὰρ, οἶμαι,
ἐστὶ τὸ καθαιρεῖσθαι λέγειν τὸν τοῖχον αὐ- τοῦ. Πέπαυται δὲ καὶ ἅπας προφητῶν
ἁγίων ὁ ἐπ' αὐτοῖς λόγος, καὶ ὑετοῦ δίκην ἀνασχὼν τρόπον τινά· καὶ διαλελοίπασιν
αἱ τῶν ἁγίων φωναί· καὶ τοῦτο, οἶμαι, ἐστὶ τὸ δι' ἑνὸς αὐτοῖς εἰρημένον παρὰ Θεοῦ·
"6Ἰδοὺ ἡμέραι ἔρχονται, λέγει Κύριος, καὶ ἐπάξω λι- μὸν ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν, οὐ λιμὸν
ἄρτου, οὐδὲ δίψαν ὕδατος· ἀλλὰ λιμὸν τοῦ ἀκοῦσαι λόγον Κυρίου. Καὶ ἀπὸ Ἀνα-
τολῶν ἕως καὶ ∆υσμῶν περιδραμοῦνται ζητοῦντες τὸν λόγον Κυρίου, καὶ οὐ μὴ
εὕρωσι."6 Καὶ ταυτὶ μὲν, ὡς ἔφην, τοῖς ἐξ Ἰσραὴλ συμβέβηκεν, καὶ μάλα εἰκότως.
Ἀπεώσαντο γὰρ αὐτοὶ τὸν τῶν δυνάμεων Κύριον, τὸν κατάρδοντα νοητῶς ψυχὰς
καὶ καρδίας, καὶ καταπιαίνοντα δρόσοις ταῖς πνευματικαῖς· ὧν καὶ ὁ μακάριος
∆αβὶδ διεμέμνητο λέγων· "6Ὡς δρό- σος Ἑρμὼν καταβαίνουσα ἐπὶ τὰ ὄρη Σιών."6
Ἐγή-γερται δὲ ἀμπελὼν ἀντ' ἐκείνου νέος, ὁ τῶν διὰ πί- στεως κεκλημένων εἰς
ἁγιασμόν. Καὶ περὶ αὐτῶν φησιν ὁ Νυμφίος ὁ ἐξ οὐρανοῦ, τοῦτ' ἔστι Χριστός· Αἱ
ἄμπελοι κυπρίζουσιν, ἔδωκαν ὀσμήν. Καὶ αὐτὸς μέν ἐστι ἡ πρώτη τε καὶ παναγία,
καὶ ἀληθὴς ἄμπε- λος. Ἀπηρτήμεθα δὲ αὐτοῦ ἡμεῖς κλημάτων δίκην, τῆς παρ' αὐτοῦ
ζωοποιοῦ πιότητος ἀναπιμπλάμενοι. Καὶ γοῦν ἔφασκεν ἐναργῶς· "6Ἐγώ εἰμι ἡ
ἄμπελος ἀληθὴς, καὶ ὁ Πατήρ μου γεωργός ἐστι· πᾶν κλῆμα ἐν ἐμοὶ μὴ φέρον
καρπὸν αἴρει αὐτὸ, καὶ πᾶν τὸ φέ- 70.144 ρον καρπὸν καθαίρει αὐτὸ, ἵνα καρπὸν
πλείονα φέ- ρῃ."6 Ἐπειδὴ δὲ αὐτῷ προσπεφύκαμεν δι' οἰκειότη- τος, δῆλον ὅτι τῆς
πνευματικῆς, ἀποτετελέσμεθα καρποφόροι· καὶ πρός γε τοῦτο ἡμᾶς ἐμπεδοῖ λέγων
αὐτός· "6Μείνατε ἐν ἐμοὶ, κἀγὼ ἐν ὑμῖν. Καθὼς τὸ κλῆμα οὐ δύναται καρπὸν φέρειν
ἀφ' ἑαυτοῦ, ἐὰν μὴ μείνῃ ἐν τῇ ἀμπέλῳ· οὕτως οὐδὲ ὑμεῖς, ἐὰν μὴ ἐν ἐμοὶ μείνητε.
Ἐγώ εἰμι ἡ ἄμπελος, ὑμεῖς δὲ τὰ κλή- ματα· ὁ μένων ἐν ἐμοὶ, κἀγὼ ἐν αὐτῷ, οὗτος
φέρει καρπὸν πολὺν, ὅτι χωρὶς ἐμοῦ οὐ δύνασθε ποιεῖν οὐδέν."6 Χρῆναι δὲ οὖν
ἔγωγέ φημι προσερηρεῖσθαι δεῖν διὰ πίστεως καὶ ἀγάπης καὶ τῆς εἰς πᾶν ὁτιοῦν
εὐπειθείας τῇ ἀμπέλῳ τῇ ἀληθινῇ, τοῦτ' ἔστι, Χρι- στῷ. Αὐτὸς γὰρ ἡμᾶς ἀποφανεῖ
καρποφόρους, αὐτὸς περιθήσει φραγμὸν, καὶ ἐγερεῖ τὸ τεῖχος, καὶ ἀπο- στή
pass_a_gloss: [...] Israel has completed without holy prophets. For they became captives at times, and went off into the country of the Persians and Medes together with women and dearest ones. But not without holy prophets did they go down into Egypt, the Babylonians having at a time taken the famous Jerusalem, but the prophet Jeremiah was with them, serving the words from above and from God. But since they acted drunkenly outrageous toward Christ, they have continued empty of hedge, and all their safety has fallen. For this, I think, is the saying that its wall is pulled down. And the whole word of holy prophets upon them has ceased, and as rain held back in a certain manner; and the voices of the saints have left off; and this, I think, is the thing said to them through one by God: Behold days are coming, says the Lord, and I will bring a famine upon the land, not a famine of bread nor thirst of water; but a famine of hearing word of the Lord. And from East as far as West they will run around seeking the word of the Lord, and will surely not find. And these things, as I said, have befallen those from Israel, and very fittingly. For they themselves thrust away the Lord of the powers, the one watering spiritually souls and hearts, and fattening them with the spiritual dews; which the blessed David also remembered, saying: As dew of Hermon coming down upon the mountains of Zion. And a new vineyard has been raised in place of that one, that of those called through faith into sanctification. And about them the Bridegroom from heaven, that is, Christ, says: The vines blossom, they gave smell. And he himself is the first and all-holy and true vine. And we hang from him like branches, filled with the life-making fatness from him. And indeed he was saying clearly: I am the true vine, and my Father is the farmer; every branch in me not bearing fruit he takes away, and every one bearing fruit he cleanses, so that it may bear more fruit. And since we have grown onto him through kinship, clearly the spiritual, we have been made fruit-bearing; and toward this he himself makes us firm, saying: Remain in me, and I in you. As the branch cannot bear fruit from itself, unless it remains in the vine; so neither you, unless you remain in me. I am the vine, you the branches; the one remaining in me and I in him, this one bears much fruit, because without me you can do nothing. It is needed then, I say, to be firmly set through faith and love and the obedience in anything whatever upon the true vine, that is, Christ. For he will show us fruit-bearing, he will put around a hedge, and raise the wall, and will dr[ive off] [the section breaks off].
pass_b_english: … Israel has passed without holy prophets. At times they were taken captive and went off to the land of the Persians and Medes together with their wives and those dearest to them. Yet when the Babylonians had at one time taken the famous Jerusalem, they did not go down into Egypt without holy prophets: the prophet Jeremiah was with them, ministering the words that came from above and from God.

But since they raged against Christ, they have remained without a hedge, and all their security has fallen. This, I think, is what is meant by saying that its wall is pulled down (Isaiah 5:5). Every word of the holy prophets to them has ceased, held back in a way like rain (Isaiah 5:6), and the voices of the saints have failed.

And this, I think, is what God said to them through one of the prophets: “Behold, days are coming, says the Lord, when I will send a famine on the land, not a famine of bread or a thirst for water, but a famine of hearing the word of the Lord. And from the east to the west they will run about seeking the word of the Lord, and they will not find it” (Amos 8:11–12).

These things, as I said, have befallen those of Israel, and with good reason. For they thrust away the Lord of hosts, who waters souls and hearts in a spiritual way and enriches them with spiritual dews; blessed David also recalled these, saying, “Like the dew of Hermon that comes down on the mountains of Zion” (Psalm 133:3).

In its place a new vineyard has been raised up, made up of those called through faith to holiness. Of them the Bridegroom from heaven, that is, Christ, says: “The vines are in blossom; they have given their fragrance” (Song of Songs 2:13). He himself is the first, all-holy, and true vine, and we hang from him like branches, filled with the life-giving richness that comes from him.

Indeed, he said plainly: “I am the true vine, and my Father is the vinedresser. Every branch in me that does not bear fruit he takes away, and every branch that bears fruit he prunes, so that it may bear more fruit” (John 15:1–2).

Since we have grown onto him through kinship, clearly a spiritual kinship, we have been made fruitful. And he himself confirms us in this, saying: “Abide in me, and I in you. As the branch cannot bear fruit by itself unless it abides in the vine, neither can you unless you abide in me. I am the vine, you are the branches. Whoever abides in me, and I in him, bears much fruit, for apart from me you can do nothing” (John 15:4–5).
